topics.topic: Definition and enforcement of the private-network boundary for unauthenticated reads
questions: Which interfaces, peers or network controls form the trusted private-network boundary on which unauthenticated reads are allowed?
What network is considered private, who may reach it, and whether Registry binds directly to it or is reached through a trusted proxy are unspecified.
What exact network boundary qualifies as the private network, and which component is responsible for preventing unauthenticated reads from being reachable outside it?

quotes:
They reach Registry over HTTP on the host's loopback or
  private network; a service that writes holds a service token (R0-09).

Reading projects, rooms, artifacts, `validate` and `context` needs no
  credential there; every write and every read of contact data does (R0-09).

Reads of projects, rooms,
artifacts, `validate` and `context` stay open on loopback and the private
network.
judgement.divergence: One implementation exposes unauthenticated reads only through loopback or an explicitly trusted proxy/network segment; another binds Registry to interfaces reachable beyond that boundary and relies on the surrounding network. Remote callers and the owner notice whether unauthenticated project data is externally reachable.
judgement.why: The named trust boundary is still hidden behind the undefined abstraction “private network,” so State 0 has not established where its unauthenticated-read promise applies or who enforces it.

topics.topic: Mechanism, authority, lifecycle, and activation behavior for credential and instance configuration
questions: What external configuration system holds credentials, and which actor is authorized to provision, rotate and revoke the staff credential and service tokens?
Who is trusted to provision, rotate and revoke these credentials, and what happens to requests during credential replacement?
Who provisions, changes, rotates and revokes credentials and other instance configuration, through what mechanism, and whether configuration changes require restart or take effect live?

quotes:
service tokens and the staff credential, in the instance's
  protected configuration; never in a record, a log line or an answer.

Each writing service holds a service token that names it; staff hold a staff
credential. Every write needs one of them; recording, correcting, reading or
erasing a customer needs the staff credential.
judgement.divergence: One implementation lets a deployment administrator replace credentials out of band with activation on restart; another provides live configuration managed by Registry staff with overlapping old and new credentials during rotation. Operators and authenticated callers notice who can change credentials, when replacements take effect, and whether requests fail during rotation.
judgement.why: “Protected configuration” leaves both the responsible actor and the external configuration mechanism unnamed, which is within State 0's required product boundary.

topics.topic: Authority, activation, and validation of artifact-vocabulary configuration changes
questions: Is vocabulary administration an out-of-band deployment operation or a Registry action, and who is authorized to perform it?
Who changes the configured artifact vocabulary, when a change becomes active, and what observable result or failure occurs if the configuration is invalid?

judgement.why: P3 already judged the same artifact-vocabulary configuration authority, validation, and activation-lifecycle question on unchanged text.

precedent.topic: Artifact vocabulary configuration shape, identity mapping, validation, and lifecycle
quotes:
The artifact types an instance accepts, and the one owner service of each, are
a list in the instance's configuration, not in the specification: adding a type
needs no spec change.
precedent.why: Configuration shape, loading lifecycle and malformed-configuration handling are operational concerns owned by State 4.

topics.topic: Whether consumer services may create Registry identity records or write back identity corrections
questions: What does “none of them writes it back” prohibit: all service writes to project identity, only corrections of an existing snapshot, or something else?
Does the snapshot-only rule prohibit consumer services from creating projects and rooms, or only from sending cached identity data back as corrections?

quotes:
Every other service names a project by the Registry's identity and
reads that identity as a snapshot; none of them writes it back (V1-2).

today Cabinet
  Kernel and the operator also create projects and rooms, and publish artifacts as
  producers (below).

A room is created in a project and listed; it is never renamed or removed.
Nothing more is added until a consumer needs it.
judgement.why: The specific permissions expressly allow Cabinet Kernel to create projects and rooms, while the snapshot rule prohibits consumers from writing read identity snapshots back; the absence of room correction or removal reinforces that distinction.

topics.topic: Which planner services are actual Registry producers, their owner names, and their publishing authentication path
questions: Which planner service or services are actual producers, what owner-service names identify them, and do they publish with service tokens or only through staff?
Which planner service or services are producers, what names identify them, and do they actually publish through this Registry or merely appear as possible configured owners?

quotes:
Producers — any caller that publishes an artifact pointer: today
  PresuPro (estimates), Cabinet Kernel and the operator script; planners by
  name only. The pointer names its owner service, which is the authority for
  the artifact itself; Registry holds the pointer (V1-4).

A service publishing with its token
  publishes only as the service the token names; staff, and the operator
  acting as staff, publish for any owner service (R0-09).
judgement.divergence: One implementation treats a named planner service as an active producer that publishes with its own service token; another treats planners only as possible owner names whose pointers can be published by staff. The planner, staff, and Registry notice whether planner-token publication is accepted.
judgement.why: The phrase “planners by name only” leaves unnamed external actors and does not establish whether any planner actually performs the publishing action or through which stated actor path.
judgement.failure: the quoted passage of a consequential gap is not found verbatim in the texts

topics.topic: Behavior of an idempotent project-create replay after the referenced customer is erased
questions: When an equal create replay names an existing project whose referenced Customer has since been erased, does Registry return the existing project or refuse the erased customer reference?

topics.topic: Scope of Registry-owned data allowed under the identity-and-pointers-only storage boundary
questions: Is “identity and pointers only” meant to include all Registry-owned customer and lifecycle metadata, or must the storage promise be narrowed to enumerate the non-pointer facts Registry stores?

topics.topic: Whether the staff credential is shared instance-wide or separately issued per person or client
questions: Is there one shared instance-wide staff credential, one credential per staff member, or credentials issued to separate staff clients such as the frontend and operator?
